text.p: AlliedSignal Inc had a good fourth quarter and is optimistic about 1997, chief executive Lawrence A. Bossidy said in a telephone interview.

Earlier, the company said fourth quarter profits were up 16 percent, leaving the company with a 17 percent increase in annual earnings to a record $1.02 billion, or $3.61 per share -- the fifth year in which profits were up 15 percent or more.

With $1.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments following the sale of its auto brake business last year, the company has intensified the search for acquisitions, Bossidy told Reuters.
The company noted net debt (debt adjusted for surplus cash) as a percentage of total capital was 9.1 percent, down from 30.9 percent at the end of 1995.
The chief executive said AlliedSignal is confident of completing some acquisitions. The search is focused on specialty chemicals, the aerospace after market and automotive turbochargers, he said.

Bossidy said AlliedSignal will continue its high level of investment in current operations, and expects capital spending and research and development spending to again total about $1 billion for the year.

R&D outlays will again fall into the $350 to $380 million range with capital spending at roughly $750 million in both years, the executive said. About two thirds of the capital spending will be on engineered materials, followed by the company's auto and aerospace units, in that order.

Driving 1996 results were higher sales and double-digit net income increases in Aerospace engines, equipment systems and electronic systems; Automotive turbochargers, filters and spark plugs and the North American aftermarket; and Engineered Materials polymers, fluorines and specialty chemicals.
Sales totaled $14.0 billion last year, an increase of 8 percent when revenues from the auto brake unit are excluded.
The company said it expects to generate earnings growth of 13 to 17 percent this year.

Both net income and net income per share will show that growth, Bossidy said, explaining the company buys back stock to cover any needs for new shares, adding it plans to buy about 7 million shares this year as it did in 1996.
